key_insight: Equilibrated flux estimators can still provide a guaranteed, fully computable upper bound for finite-element energy error even on coarse or badly distorted meshes, without shape-regularity assumptions.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a reliable way to quantify simulation error for real-world geometries and poor-quality meshes, where classical a posteriori theory may not apply.
method: Use equilibrated fluxes to bound the energy-norm discretization error.
Exploit only local cell geometry via the Poincaré constant, not global mesh regularity.
Leverage the Payne–Weinberger bound on convex cells: Poincaré constant ≤ h_K/π.
evidence_signal: The abstract argues analytically that reliability is preserved under distortion, with the main impact of poor mesh quality being reduced local efficiency rather than loss of guaranteed bounds.
watch_item: The estimator may become pessimistic on highly distorted meshes, so a valid bound does not necessarily mean a sharp error estimate.
paper_title: A posteriori error estimation for coarse or distorted meshes
